title: Count the lines
prompt:
Count the lines and the bytes on standard input without `scanf` or `getchar`: ask the operating system for the bytes yourself with the `read` system call. With the stdin box as given the program prints `lines: 3, bytes: 34`.

`read` is service 63. Put the file descriptor in `x0` (0 is standard input), the buffer address in `x1`, the most bytes you want in `x2`, and 63 in `x8`, then run `svc 0`. The answer in `x0` is how many bytes actually arrived, which can be fewer than you asked for. An answer of 0 means the input is finished.

So read into the 64-byte `buf` in a loop: add each answer to the byte count, and count the newline bytes (value 10) among the bytes that read just delivered. Only those: whatever sits past them in `buf` is left over from an earlier read. A line counts when its newline arrives, so text whose last line has no newline has one line fewer than it looks.

The stdin box stands in for running the program with `< file` on a server: once its text runs out, `read` answers 0. If a run ever sits waiting for more input instead, Ctrl-D in the console's input line ends it.

## what is checked

- the count line for the text in the stdin box, and for more inputs you cannot see (short, empty, and longer than the buffer)
- the program exits cleanly
- the input comes through system calls (`svc` present, no `getchar`)
starter:
// count the lines and bytes on standard input, reading it in chunks with svc
define(fp, x29)
define(lr, x30)

define(lines_r, x19)
define(bytes_r, x20)
define(got_r, x21)
define(buf_r, x22)

define(STDIN, 0)
define(SYS_READ, 63)
define(BUF_SIZE, 64)

.data
fmt_out:    .string "lines: %ld, bytes: %ld\n"

.bss
buf:        .skip 64                        // BUF_SIZE bytes

.text
        .balign 4
        .global main
main:
        stp     fp, lr, [sp, -16]!
        mov     fp, sp

        mov     lines_r, 0
        mov     bytes_r, 0
        ldr     buf_r, =buf

        // TODO: repeat until read answers 0 (end of input) or less:
        //   read up to BUF_SIZE bytes from STDIN into buf, add the number
        //   of bytes it delivered to bytes_r, and count the newline bytes
        //   (value 10) among just those bytes into lines_r.

        ldr     x0, =fmt_out
        mov     x1, lines_r
        mov     x2, bytes_r
        bl      printf

        mov     w0, 0
        ldp     fp, lr, [sp], 16
        ret
